title: Certify v0.13.0: certified ZEFOZ brackets for ¹⁶⁷Er³⁺:Y₂SiO₅ — existence, curvature and stationary-point type of every published clock transition, with a pre-registered kill of the completeness question
description: Zero-first-order-Zeeman (ZEFOZ) points are the magnetic fields at which a transition frequency is stationary, and they are what makes a rare-earth-doped crystal usable as a long-lived quantum memory: the predicted coherence time is set by the curvature of the frequency surface at such a point. Published ZEFOZ atlases are produced by grid search plus Newton refinement, and their authors state that the number of points found depends on the initial grid. This release certifies the atlas of ¹⁶⁷Er³⁺:Y₂SiO₅ (Matsuura et al., Phys. Rev. B 113, 085421 (2026)). For each of the twenty published nonzero-field points across both crystallographic sites, a certificate re-checkable by a standard-library Python program establishes, in exact rational and outward-rounded interval arithmetic: transition brackets of width 4e-10 MHz at an exactly specified rational field; a certified gradient bound |grad f| <= 3.2e-37 MHz/mT; two-sided brackets of width <= 2.1e-15 on all three eigenvalues of the 3x3 frequency Hessian — the quantity that sets the predicted T2 — together with its certified signature, showing every published point to be a saddle or a local maximum and none a minimum; and, by a Krawczyk contraction with a rigorous Kato/Cauchy third-derivative bound, the existence and local uniqueness of an exact stationary point within 2.9e-14 mT of the stated field. At zero field an exact symbolic time-reversal identity over Q[sqrt7,sqrt12,sqrt15] certifies that all 120 transitions of both sites are stationary. The completeness question — whether the published list is the whole list — carried a pre-registered kill condition, and it fired: measured certified branch-and-bound exclusion gives a strict lower bound above 7.9e5 laptop-hours per site, so completeness is reported dead at this scale with the obstruction quantified and the open route named. Three errata in the reference are documented and versioned, including two Table-5 frequencies that disagree with their own stationary points by -2.74 and -4.34 MHz. Adversarially reviewed before release. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author.
